summary: The RLS policy on public.invoices uses `using (true)`, so any authenticated user can read every invoice. Restrict it to the owner, for example `auth.uid() = user_id`.
SQL injection: the user-controlled `q` and `sort` parameters are interpolated directly into `$queryRawUnsafe`. Use parameterized `$queryRaw` and an allowlist of sort columns.

The email input has no programmatic label (placeholder only), so it has no accessible name for screen readers (WCAG 1.3.1/4.1.2). Add a <label> or aria-label, plus type="email" and autocomplete="email".

The checkout endpoint creates a PaymentIntent with the amount and currency the client sends, so a buyer can pay any price they choose. Compute the amount on the server from the cart or price IDs, and require authentication and validation.
The search term is parameterized and its LIKE wildcards are escaped, and the sort comes from a fixed allowlist of Prisma.sql fragments. No issues found.
A Supabase service_role JWT is hardcoded in frontend code. It bypasses RLS and gives anyone full database access. Revoke and rotate the key now, and use the anon or publishable key on the client.

Open, confirmed high-severity finding AG-001: a runtime test shows any signed-in user can read another user's invoice (200 instead of 404) at the release commit. Green unit tests do not override this, so the release is NO-GO until it is fixed and retested.

saveNote retries a non-idempotent POST immediately with no backoff or idempotency key, does not retry on network errors (fetch rejects), and returns silently after three failures, so the caller assumes the note was saved. Throw or return an error on final failure, add backoff and an idempotency key, and set Content-Type.

readInvoices uses the admin database client to return every invoice with no user or tenant scoping or authorization check, so whoever can call this tool can read all customers' invoices. Scope the query to the authenticated user and use a least-privilege client.
Only a Supabase publishable key is exposed, which is meant to be public in client code. No issues found.
The route authenticates the user and returns 404 unless the invoice belongs to them. No issues found.
The invoice route has no authentication or ownership check, so anyone can fetch any invoice by ID (IDOR). Require a user and return 404 unless invoice.userId matches.
Documentation-only typo fix in README.md. No issues found.

Check-then-update race: concurrent requests can both see redeemed=false and redeem the same coupon more than once. Use an atomic conditional update (updateMany where code and redeemed=false, then check the count) or a transaction.

Premium is unlocked just by rendering the success page, without checking with the payment provider, so anyone can visit the URL and get premium for free. Grant entitlements on the server from a verified payment webhook or session.
The RLS select policy limits invoice reads to the owning user (auth.uid() = user_id). No issues found.

The audit has an open, confirmed critical finding (a service-role credential in client code), and the critical mandatory 'secrets' check is FAIL, so the recorded GO is not supported. The release is NO-GO until the key is rotated, removed from the client, and the check is re-run.

Static review shows the route requires a user and returns 404 unless invoice.userId matches, but with no database, test run, or staging environment, the ownership check could not be run. Record it as NOT TESTED, not PASS.
